record.original_question: For the core-collapse supernova subclasses SNIIb, SNIIn, and SNIIL, are their progenitor masses located in the apparent 16–20 solar-mass gap between measured Type IIP progenitors of about 8–16 solar masses and Type Ib/c lower limits above about 20 solar masses, or are those explosion types mainly determined by other parameters such as binarity or rotation?

evidence.quote: Type IIP SN progenitors, leading to the identification of red supergiant progenitors and to explicit mass determinations for about a dozen SNe, which fall in the range ∼ 8M⊙ to ∼ 16M⊙.
The few lower limits indicate that the targeted SNIb/c had progenitors with masses above ∼20 M⊙.
Still we don’t know much about the remaining multiplicity of CC-SNe, such as SNIIb, SIIn, SNIIL.

The progenitor mass estimates for SNIIP and SNIb/c leaves unanswered the question "are the progenitors masses of SNIIn, SNIIL, SNIIb falling in the apparent gap 16-20 M⊙ or are these SN explosions mostly determined by some other parameter, such as binarity, rotation, etc?"

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Core-collapse supernovae are commonly divided into subclasses by their observed spectra and light curves, including: Type IIP (hydrogen-rich, plateau light curve), Type IIL (hydrogen-rich, linearly declining light curve), Type IIn (hydrogen-rich with narrow emission lines indicating dense circumstellar material), Type IIb (hydrogen layer present at early times but rapidly disappearing, becoming helium-dominated), and Types Ib/Ic (hydrogen-poor, with Ic also helium-poor).

Direct imaging of pre-explosion progenitors has yielded zero-age main-sequence (ZAMS) mass estimates of approximately 8 M_⊙ to 16 M_⊙ for about a dozen Type IIP progenitors (identified as red supergiants), while available lower limits for Type Ib/Ic progenitors place their masses above approximately 20 M_⊙. This leaves an apparent gap in the directly measured progenitor masses in the range 16 M_⊙ ≲ M ≲ 20 M_⊙.

Determine, for each of the subclasses Type IIb, Type IIn, and Type IIL: do their progenitors have ZAMS masses lying in the apparent 16–20 M_⊙ gap between measured Type IIP and Type Ib/c progenitors, or are these explosion types instead primarily determined by other physical parameters such as binary companion interaction or stellar rotation rather than by initial mass alone?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent direct-detection and statistical studies have made substantial progress: Type IIb progenitors (e.g., SN 1993J, SN 2011dh, SN 2013df) are now strongly favored to arise from interacting binary systems with moderate ZAMS masses (~12–17 M_⊙), supporting binarity rather than the mass gap. Type IIL studies (e.g., Anderson et al. and Hα-association statistics) suggest progenitor masses similar to or slightly above SNIIP, with envelope stripping by binarity or metallicity playing a role. Type IIn remains the most heterogeneous and least understood, with evidence for both very massive (LBV-like) and lower-mass progenitors. Thus the question is partially resolved, with binarity now considered a major determining factor, but a definitive mass distribution for each subclass is not yet established.

status_evidence.title: Binary progenitor models of type IIb supernovae
status_evidence.snippet: SNIIb progenitors modeled as interacting binaries with moderate-mass components.
status_evidence.claim: Type IIb progenitors are best explained by binary interaction rather than single very massive stars.

status_evidence.title: Progenitor mass constraints for core-collapse supernovae from correlations with host galaxy star formation
status_evidence.snippet: SNIIL show association with Hα similar to SNIIP, while SNIb/c trace more massive populations.
status_evidence.claim: Statistical studies place SNIIL progenitors near the SNIIP mass range, suggesting other parameters drive the IIL morphology.

status_evidence.title: The direct identification of core-collapse supernova progenitors
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews directly identified progenitors and the inferred mass ranges for various CC-SN subtypes.
status_evidence.claim: The progenitor mass distributions for IIb, IIn, IIL remain only partially constrained, with binarity playing a key role.
